input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When ANSI stripping is triggered, the code calls `.strip()` on the result of `strip_ansi(text)`, which removes leading and trailing whitespace from the prompt. The title only says to strip ANSI codes.
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt like "Name: " or "Continue? [y/N]: " with a trailing space, or one with leading indentation, when the stream is not a tty or color is disabled, as in piped output or CliRunner. The trailing space separating the prompt from user input is dropped, so output shows "Name:value" and the prompt text changes between tty and non-tty runs. Existing tests and users that compare prompt output will see different text.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation: an extra .strip() after strip_ansi drops the trailing space of the prompt. It also gives the same trigger, a non-color stream such as piped output or CliRunner, and the same effect, output that differs between tty and non-tty runs.
